title: Chapter 41 — The Trade Channel: Why It Exists and What It's Worth
intro: The second engine — what trade business is and the career mathematics of an account book.

sections.title: The Second Engine
sections.content:
A builder or designer relationship is not one sale — it is 10-50 sales per year. One strong builder account can be worth more than 200 walk-in ups. Treat them accordingly.

Trade business is the second revenue engine for any appliance retailer. Retail is transactional — customers come in, buy, and leave. Trade is relational — accounts stay for years and produce predictable, repeatable revenue.

sections.title: What Trade Buyers Want
sections.content:
Builders want consistent pricing they can budget against, reliable delivery timing because their schedule depends on yours, a single point of contact who knows their projects, package pricing for multi-unit specs, same-day quote turnaround, and someone who understands construction timelines and rough-in requirements.

Designers want product knowledge deeper than their own, finish and panel-ready options, integration specs and cutout dimensions, someone who can coordinate with the builder and the client, and a partner, not a vendor.

sections.title: The Career Mathematics
sections.content:
A trade specialist with 15 active builder accounts averaging 3 projects each per year at $5,000 average ticket generates $225,000 in annual revenue from trade alone. Add retail floor sales on top and you have a $350,000+ producing rep.

The math gets better over time. Accounts compound. Referrals multiply. A builder who uses you on 3 projects this year refers you to another builder next year. Within 3 years, a dedicated trade rep can build a book that generates income independent of floor traffic.
